To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
isolate-rearing and brief encounters with conspecifics increase shock-induced fighting.

(1) the effects of social isolation on aggression are not due to the absence of social interaction; (2) brief encounters can reduce shock-induced aggression; and (3) the effects of encounters depend on the gender of the conspecific with which the subjects interact.
The effects of early rearing conditions on aggression were modified by the type of early social interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of early social interactions on the development of shock-induced aggression in mice.
the effects of early social interaction on later aggression in male mice.
the effects of social experience on aggressive behavior in the mouse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of rearsin on shock-induced aggression in mice is mediated by social interaction and that the effects of social interaction are mediated by the sex of the opponent.
the social environment of early development has a significant influence upon the development of aggressive tendencies in mice.
social experience, whether in isolation or in groups, is an important factor in the development of aggressive behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the social environment of the young mouse can have a significant influence on later behavior.
social isolation, especially during the preweaning period, is a major factor in the development of shock-induced aggressiveness in male mice.
the effects of reared condition and brief encounters are cumulative in their effects on shock-induced aggression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
early social experience can have long-term effects on behavior.
early life experiences have long-lasting effects on behavior.
the social environment can have a powerful influence on the expression of shock-induced fighting.
